title: Choice Strength in Baire, Urysohn, Stone, and Tychonoff

items.title: Dependent multiple choice in finite-level tree form

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: DMC says every pruned serial tree has a pruned subtree with nonempty finite levels; equivalently, there are coherent nonempty finite successor menus at every level.
items.proof_plan: Define the R-chain tree, levels, pruning, predecessors, and the coherent-menu convention used below.
items.axiom_base: ZF; DMC is the principle defined

items.title: The tree and successor-menu formulations of DMC are equivalent

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Over ZF, the finite-level subtree and coherent finite successor-menu forms of DMC are equivalent.
items.proof_plan: Take levels in one direction. Conversely tag menu elements by stage and close each finite menu under its finitely many predecessors; finite unions and images of finite sets are finite in ZF, and coherence gives pruning.

items.title: A nonempty countable set has a padded enumeration in ZF

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: In ZF, every nonempty at-most-countable set D is the range of a sequence s:N→D. The empty set is treated separately and is not asserted to be the range of an N-indexed sequence.
items.proof_plan: Apply the published choice-free equivalence between a nonempty at-most-countable set and a surjective image of N. Its forward proof is explicit: if D is equipotent with N, use the witnessing bijection; if D is finite nonempty, let e:m→D be the witnessing bijection, put d*=e(0), and define s(n)=e(n) for n<m and s(n)=d* for n≥m. This is one finite case distinction on one supplied witness and uses no family choice. If D is empty, do not manufacture a sequence into D; the downstream Baire proof handles the empty ambient space before invoking this lemma.

items.title: Separable complete metric spaces are Baire in ZF

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: In ZF, every separable complete metric space is Baire.
items.proof_plan: If X is empty the Baire conclusion is immediate. Otherwise separability supplies one at-most-countable dense D, which is nonempty because X is; the preceding lemma converts that single witness, with its finite padding case explicit, into a fixed dense sequence. Recursively take the lexicographically least center-index/rational-radius pair whose closed ball lies in the previous open set intersected with the next dense open set and whose radius is at most 2^(-n-2). Existence follows from density and metric regularity; least-number choice is definable. The centers are Cauchy and completeness puts their limit in all nested closed balls.
items.axiom_base: ZF; the one supplied dense set, explicit padding, and least-number selection replace DC

items.title: Metacompactness: every open cover has a point-finite open refinement

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Definitions of refinement and effective metacompactness, printed pp. 8-9

items.title: DMC makes every compact Hausdorff space Baire

references.title: David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)
Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness

items.statement: ZF+DMC proves every compact Hausdorff space Baire.
items.proof_plan: Use Fremlin Proposition 2 verbatim. The Hausdorff hypothesis and the preceding compact-Hausdorff theorem first make X regular (indeed normal); this is the exact separation input. For dense open G_n and nonempty open G put G'_k=intersection_{j<k}G_j and let V be the nonempty open subsets of G. Declare U succeeds V when some k has closure(V) contained in U intersect G'_k while U is not contained in G'_k. Unless an open subset already lies in every G_k, regularity makes this relation serial. DMC supplies finite menus V_n; prune them to coherent nonempty finite menus V'_n. Induction on n shows every member of V'_n lies in G'_n. The finite unions W_n of their closures are nonempty closed and decreasing, so countable compactness, hence compactness, gives a point of G intersect intersection_n G_n. All selections are finite or supplied by DMC.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DMC; DMC supplies coherent finite refinement menus

items.title: Compact Hausdorff Baire implies DMC

references.title: David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)
Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness

items.statement: Over ZF, if every compact Hausdorff space is Baire, then DMC holds.
items.proof_plan: Reproduce Fremlin Theorem 4, including its separation bookkeeping. Give the tree T the discrete topology, so it is locally compact Hausdorff; the one-point-compactification theorem makes A=T union {infinity} compact Hausdorff. The product topology and Hausdorff-product lemma make X=A^omega Hausdorff, and the hereditary lemma makes its closed subspace K Hausdorff. Here K is the closed set whose non-infinity coordinates form an increasing T-chain. If K is compact, it is therefore within the assumed compact-Hausdorff Baire class, and the open dense sets G_n={x in K: some non-infinity coordinate occurs at or after n} have a common point, giving a branch. If K is not compact, start with a downward-directed family E of nonempty closed subsets of X with empty intersection, enlarged by all forbidden-comparability complements. Recursively adjoin the infinity fibre at coordinate n whenever every projection contains infinity. For the resulting E*, let D be the coordinates whose infinity fibre is absent and F_n=intersection{pi_n[E]:E in E*}; each F_n is finite nonempty. Prove D infinite, since otherwise fixing the finitely many F_n and infinity elsewhere gives a cluster point of E*. Directedness and the forbidden-comparability complements show that for m<n in D every s in F_m has an extension in F_n. Enumerate D and prune successive F_n to coherent nonempty finite levels; their downward closure is a height-omega subtree with finite levels. Lemma 3 converts this tree form to DMC. This is a complete ZF dichotomy and does not assume the product X compact.

items.title: Compact Hausdorff Baire is equivalent to DMC

references.title: Fossy and Morillon, The Baire category property and some notions of compactness
David H. Fremlin, Dependent multiple choice and Baire's theorem (following Fossy and Morillon)

items.statement: Over ZF, every compact Hausdorff space is Baire iff DMC.
items.proof_plan: Combine the preceding two proof-bearing directions. The forward proof spends exactly DMC; the reverse uses the compact/noncompact dichotomy for K and no choice principle. No Recorded catalogue item is used.

items.title: DC is equivalent to Baireness of compact-Hausdorff products

references.title: Horst Herrlich and Kyriakos Keremedis, Products, the Baire category theorem, and the axiom of dependent choice
references.locator: Definitions and Theorem 4, journal pp. 771-775 (scan pp. 1333-1337)

items.statement: Over ZF, DC is equivalent to every product, including the empty product, of compact Hausdorff spaces being Baire.
items.proof_plan: Forward: reproduce Herrlich-Keremedis Theorem 4. The empty product is Baire. In a nonempty product fix x. For a basic open B and dense opens D_n, use the regular pseudo-bases of compact Hausdorff factors to define the serial relation on quadruples (n,F,(B_i),(mathcal B_i)): the next finite-support cylinder has closures nested coordinatewise and lies in B intersect D_n. DC gives a chain. Its support F=union_n F_n is countable under DC; for each i in F the nested closures form a countably based regular filter meeting every pseudo-base, hence have nonempty intersection. Countable Choice, implied by DC, chooses b_i from these intersections, while x supplies off-support coordinates. The resulting product point lies in B intersect intersection_n D_n. Reverse: for a serial relation on A, each alpha A=A union {infinity} is compact Hausdorff and the assumed countable product X=(alpha A)^omega is Baire. A^omega is the intersection of the open dense coordinate sets {x:x(n) in A}; every open dense subset of A^omega is the trace of an open dense subset of X, so A^omega is Baire. Apply the published Blair sequence-space converse to extract an R-chain. This proves DC and avoids citing Theorem 3 as a black box. The theorem makes no nonemptiness claim for a product of nonempty factors.

items.title: DMC implies Urysohn's lemma

references.title: Schechter, Urysohn's lemma and the axiom of choice

items.statement: ZF+DMC proves Urysohn's lemma for normal spaces.
items.proof_plan: At each finite dyadic stage form the serial relation of all simultaneous tuples satisfying closure(U_r) subset U_s. DMC supplies coherent finite menus. Intersect the finitely many candidates coordinatewise; finite intersections preserve openness and closure nesting. Define f by the usual dyadic infimum and verify inverse images.

items.title: DMC versus DC over ZF remains open

references.title: Morillon, Axiom of Choice

items.statement: DC implies DMC over ZF. Strictness is known in ZFA, but whether DMC implies DC in ZF is open; no ZF strictness is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Use the existing DC-to-finite-selections theorem and record Morillon's open question exactly.

items.title: Brunner's ordered Läuchli permutation models

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: Define Brunner's ordered permutation models P(A,G,I), their interval supports, and the linearly ordered Läuchli continua carried by them. Two instances are distinguished: real-ordered atoms with the ideal generated by countable compact supports for Countable Choice, and rational-ordered atoms with finite supports for the BPI separation.
items.proof_plan: Transcribe P(A,G,I), relative compactness of supports in bounded intervals, the order completion/cut construction, and strong connectedness exactly from Brunner §§1-3. Keep the real/countable-compact and rational/finite-support instances separate; no Fraenkel-Mostowski conclusion is imported without its verified support calculation.
items.axiom_base: ZFA+AC metatheory; target permutation models of ZFA

items.title: Brunner's models satisfy the required choice and Urysohn obstructions

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: The real-ordered countable-compact-support model satisfies Countable Choice, and both it and the rational finite-support model contain a nondegenerate compact linearly ordered normal space on which every real-valued continuous function is constant; hence Urysohn's lemma fails.
items.proof_plan: Follow Brunner §3.4(b), without replacing the supports by their generally noncompact union. A countable family (F_n) in the real-ordered model has one common compact support e. In the ground ZFA+AC universe choose x_n in F_n and a compact support e_n for x_n. For every n construct Brunner's increasing permutation p_n in Fix(e): on each component interval of the complement of e, keep the endpoints fixed and compress the relevant pieces of e_n into separated intervals whose diameters tend to zero (the §3.4(b) 1/(n+1) construction). The intervals accumulate only at points of e, so f=e union union_n p_n(e_n) is closed and bounded, hence compact. Because p_n fixes e it fixes F_n, so y_n=p_n(x_n) lies in F_n; because p_n(e_n) supports y_n, the single compact f supports the whole sequence (y_n). This proves Countable Choice in the symmetric model. For the topology, use §3.3: relative compactness of every support in bounded intervals lets a support-fixing order automorphism move any two unsupported points through the same interval. The orbit argument forces every symmetric continuous map from the completed ordered continuum to the reals to be constant. The order topology supplies Hausdorffness and compactness; the compact-Hausdorff theorem supplies normality. Its two endpoints are distinct closed sets, and an Urysohn separator would be a nonconstant continuous map, contradiction.
items.axiom_base: ZFA inside the two specified permutation models

items.title: Extreme amenability yields BPI in finite-support permutation models

references.title: Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups

items.statement: Let G act on atoms with the finite-support filter. If every pointwise stabilizer of a finite atom set is extremely amenable in the pointwise-convergence topology, then the associated permutation model satisfies BPI.
items.proof_plan: Let B be a nondegenerate Boolean algebra in the permutation model and fix a finite support E, so H=Fix(E) acts on B. In the ZFA+AC metatheory, the set S(B) of prime ideals is a nonempty compact Hausdorff closed subspace of 2^B by the ordinary ultrafilter lemma. The H-action on S(B) is continuous because the stabilizer in H of each b in B is open. Extreme amenability of H gives an H-fixed prime ideal P. Thus E supports P; every member of P is already hereditarily symmetric as an element of B, so P belongs to the permutation model and is a prime ideal there. This proves BPI without using a Recorded transfer claim.
items.axiom_base: ZFA+AC metatheory; target permutation model satisfies ZFA+BPI

items.title: Finite stabilizers in Aut(Q,<) are extremely amenable

references.title: Kechris, Pestov, and Todorcevic, Fraïssé limits, Ramsey theory, and topological dynamics of automorphism groups
Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups

items.statement: Aut(Q,<), and every pointwise stabilizer of a finite subset of Q, is extremely amenable in the pointwise-convergence topology.
items.proof_plan: Apply the KPT correspondence. The age of (Q,<) is the class of finite linear orders; its objects are rigid. Its Ramsey property is exactly finite Ramsey: color embeddings of the a-point order into an N-point order, identify them with a-subsets, and take a homogeneous b-subset. Hence Aut(Q,<) is extremely amenable. A finite point stabilizer is the finite direct product of automorphism groups of the open rational intervals cut out by the support, each order-isomorphic to Q; prove directly that a finite product of extremely amenable groups has a fixed point by taking fixed points one factor at a time. Therefore every required open stabilizer is extremely amenable.

items.title: The Läuchli Urysohn obstruction is injectively boundable

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: The existence of Brunner's specified normal non-Urysohn space admits an atom-blind typed transfer certificate and a fixed absolute relative-rank bound below omega+omega.
items.proof_plan: Expand ordered pairs, order cuts, the topology, closedness, normality, continuity, and real-valued function graphs into membership formulas. Carry the ordered cut space, topology, its two endpoint closed sets, and all candidate real-valued function graphs as named sorts below V_{omega+omega}(A union omega). Verify that atom images are treated opaquely, the pure real interval is fixed, and every quantified object lies in a carried sort. The same typed formula says in the target that the carried space is normal and has no separating continuous real map. This supplies the exact certificate missing from the generic transfer theorem.

items.title: Pincus transfer for BPI, Countable Choice, and injectively boundable conjunctions

references.title: David Pincus, Zermelo–Fraenkel consistency results by Fraenkel–Mostowski methods
David Pincus, Adding dependent choice
references.locator: Theorem 4 and note added in proof, p. 145

references.title: Eleftherios Tachtsis, The Boolean prime ideal theorem does not imply the extension of almost disjoint families to MAD families
references.locator: Definitions 5.2–5.3, Fact 5.4, and Theorem 5.5, printed pp. 110–111

items.statement: For a permutation model of ZFA, a finite conjunction of certified injectively boundable sentences transfers to a model of ZF; Pincus's exceptional clauses also permit BPI and Countable Choice to occur in the transferred conjunction when they hold in the permutation model. In particular, either BPI or Countable Choice may be conjoined with a certified atom-blind boundable obstruction and transferred. This does not transfer arbitrary ZFA truth, full Choice, or an uncertified sentence.
items.proof_plan: Write each ordinary obstruction in Pincus's Definition 2A5 form, using its local certificate to choose an absolute relative-rank bound, and take the maximum bound for the externally fixed finite conjunction. Apply Metatheorems 3A2–3A3 to embed the required finite relative hierarchy into an atom-free ZF model while preserving every certified conjunct. For the two exceptional positive principles use Pincus's 1977 Theorem 4 and note added in proof: BPI and AC_omega are admitted alongside the injectively boundable conjuncts, as stated explicitly in Tachtsis Theorem 5.5; Brunner §3.4(a) applies precisely the AC_omega clause to his Urysohn obstruction. Finally use finite-fragment model transfer and the verified proof-reduction theorem to obtain the syntactic Con implication. Do not treat AC_omega itself as certified injectively boundable, and do not infer transfer of arbitrary ZFA truth, full AC, or any unlisted choice principle.
items.axiom_base: Formal relative consistency from ZFA permutation models to ZF

items.title: Relative consistency of Countable Choice without Urysohn's lemma

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+Countable Choice+failure of Urysohn's lemma is consistent.
items.proof_plan: Start from the formal ZFC+GCH consistency compiler and form Brunner's real-ordered countable-compact-support permutation model. The preceding support calculation proves Countable Choice and supplies a compact linearly ordered normal Läuchli continuum with no Urysohn separator. Encode the latter by the preceding atom-blind fixed-rank certificate, and apply the explicit AC_omega clause of the Pincus transfer theorem to that conjunction; this is exactly the transfer Brunner invokes in the concluding paragraph of §3.4(a). The finite-fragment consistency compiler yields the displayed Con implication. This is an independent complete route; the inaccessible Tachtsis paper and its erratum are not load-bearing, and Countable Choice is not mislabeled as an ordinary injectively boundable sentence.

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI without Urysohn's lemma

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen
Andreas Blass, Partitions and Permutation Groups

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+BPI+failure of Urysohn's lemma is consistent.
items.proof_plan: Use rational ordered atoms, Aut(Q,<), and finite supports. The stabilizer/extreme-amenability lemmas prove BPI inside the permutation model; Brunner's interval-support theorem gives the normal ordered Läuchli continuum and the continuous-function obstruction. The explicit boundability certificate and Pincus theorem transfer their conjunction to ZF, and the formal finite-fragment compiler converts the construction to the displayed Con implication. No Recorded catalogue item is a dependency.

items.title: Brunner's endpoint obstruction also refutes bounded Tietze extension

references.title: Norbert Brunner, Geordnete Läuchli Kontinuen

items.statement: For Brunner's compact normal ordered continuum X with its distinct closed endpoint sets A and B, the continuous map g:A∪B→[0,1] that is 0 on A and 1 on B has no continuous extension to X. Consequently Con(ZF) implies both Con(ZF+Countable Choice+failure of bounded Tietze extension) and Con(ZF+BPI+failure of bounded Tietze extension).
items.proof_plan: In the closed subspace A∪B, each of A and B is clopen because it is the complement of the other closed set, so the displayed two-valued g is continuous. Any continuous extension G:X→[0,1] would equal 0 on A and 1 on B and hence would be the nonconstant Urysohn separator excluded by Brunner's lemma. The fixed-rank transfer certificate already carries X, its topology, A, B, and all candidate real-valued function graphs, so the same first-order obstruction survives the Pincus transfer. Compose separately with the established Countable Choice and BPI relative-consistency theorems; do not assert an unqualified ZF counterexample.

items.title: The Good-Tree-Watson symmetric Stone model

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice

items.statement: Fix a regular uncountable lambda in the ZFC ground model (for DC take lambda=omega_1). Let P=Fn(lambda times R times lambda times lambda,2,lambda), ordered by reverse inclusion, let B=RO(P), and use the Good-Tree-Watson automorphism group with the normal filter generated by pointwise stabilizers of subsets of lambda times R times lambda of size below lambda. Its hereditarily symmetric interpretation contains the families x_{xi,r,alpha}, X_{xi,r}, R_xi and M={R_xi:xi<lambda}.
items.proof_plan: Start from the regular-lambda generalization stated immediately after Good-Tree-Watson Theorem 3, rather than conflating it with the finite-support omega-index presentation of Theorems 1-3. Transcribe §2's reverse-inclusion forcing order and Boolean completion with omega replaced by lambda and every support bound replaced by <lambda. Automorphisms send (xi,r,alpha) to (xi,rho(r),alpha') with rho either a reflection or the identity; pointwise stabilizers of <lambda-sized subsets generate a normal <lambda-complete filter because lambda is regular. Repeat Claims 1.1-1.2 to verify the action on the four displayed canonical names and hereditary symmetry. This is an atom-free symmetric forcing construction, not a Fraenkel-Mostowski model.
items.axiom_base: ZFC metatheory; target symmetric model ZF+DC

items.title: The Good-Tree-Watson symmetric model is closed under omega-sequences from the full extension

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Theorem 3 and the regular-lambda generalization immediately following it, printed p. 6; reduction to Jech Lemma 8.5

references.title: Thomas J. Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.statement: In the regular-lambda Good-Tree-Watson construction, if beta<lambda and g belongs to the full P-generic extension, has domain beta, and every value g(xi) belongs to the symmetric model N, then g belongs to N. In particular, for lambda=omega_1 the conclusion holds for omega-sequences.
items.proof_plan: Repeat Jech Lemma 8.5 with the Good-Tree-Watson regular-lambda data. First P is <lambda-closed: the union of a descending beta-chain of conditions, beta<lambda, has domain of size <lambda by ground-model choice and regularity. Closure gives in the ground model a function f:beta->HS of names with g(xi)=i_G(f(xi)). Choose for each f(xi) a support e_xi of size <lambda. Then e=union_{xi<beta} e_xi has size <lambda by regularity; fix(e) fixes every f(xi), hence fixes the graph name f, whose subnames are hereditarily symmetric. Thus f itself is hereditarily symmetric and g=i_G(f) belongs to N. This is exactly the support-union argument available in the paper's regular-lambda construction; no unsupported orbit-mixing argument and no false finite-support closure claim is used.
items.axiom_base: ZFC metatheory; closure conclusion inside the symmetric extension

items.title: The symmetric Stone model has no componentwise proper selector

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Claim 1.3, printed pp. 4-5, with the regular-lambda replacement specified after Theorem 3 on printed p. 6

items.statement: No symmetric function chooses a nonempty proper subset of every distinguished metric component.
items.proof_plan: Take a <lambda-sized support e for a supposed selector. Regularity makes the projection of e to the first coordinate have size <lambda, so choose xi<lambda outside it. Decide one selected and one unselected point of R_xi, and apply an e-fixing automorphism exchanging their indistinguishable coordinates. Symmetry preserves the name but reverses the decisions. This is Claim 1.3 with finite/omega replaced uniformly by <lambda/lambda, exactly as directed in the paragraph after Theorem 3.

items.title: Relative consistency of DC with failure of Stone's theorem

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice
references.locator: Theorems 2-4, printed pp. 5-8, especially the regular-lambda generalization after Theorem 3 on printed p. 6

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+DC with a zero-dimensional metrizable nonparacompact space is consistent.
items.proof_plan: Take lambda=omega_1 of the ZFC+GCH ground and use the paper's regular-lambda construction. Inside the full ZFC extension, DC builds a chain for any serial relation in N; the <lambda-sequence closure lemma returns its omega-sequence to N, proving DC. Give the metric sum of the R_xi, xi<lambda, and repeat the explicit cover calculation from Theorem 2 coordinatewise. A locally finite refinement canonically yields a nonempty proper subset of every R_xi, contradicting the generalized Claim 1.3; no countable family of components is used. Repeat Theorem 4 with the rational-translation/clopen Q_xi and verify Claims 4.1-4.3 under the same uniform replacements omega by lambda and finite support by <lambda support. Finally carry this uniformly through every finite target fragment and apply the formal consistency compiler from Con(ZF) via ZFC+GCH. This separates semantic construction from the syntactic Con conclusion.
items.axiom_base: Formal relative consistency over ZF; target ZF+DC

items.title: Corson's ordered-rational permutation model

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: The atoms are the ordered rational Urysohn metric space; automorphisms preserve order and metric, and finite supports generate the symmetric model.
items.proof_plan: Record the rational ordered Urysohn metric space U_Q^<, its order-and-metric automorphism group, the finite-support normal filter, and the resulting ZFA permutation universe. Do not conflate Aut(U_Q^<) with Aut(Q,<); its extreme amenability is supplied separately through the ordered-metric Fraïssé/Ramsey theorem.

items.title: Corson's rational metric space is not metacompact

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: In Corson's permutation model, the rational Urysohn metric space has an open cover with no point-finite refinement.
items.proof_plan: Use Corson §2.2. The cover is by rational-radius balls of the displayed small radii. Assume a point-finite refinement and fix a finite support E for it. Choose a point outside E and one refining member containing it. Ordered-metric ultrahomogeneity extends the finite partial isometries which fix E and the chosen point while moving the unsupported witness through infinitely many rational positions. Symmetry returns infinitely many distinct refinement members through the fixed point, contradicting point-finiteness. Follow the paper's finite metric-extension inequalities explicitly; there is no Proposition 7.

items.title: Aut(U_Q^<) is extremely amenable

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem
Nešetřil, Ramsey classes and homogeneous structures
references.locator: Ramsey theorem for finite ordered rational metric spaces

references.title: Kechris, Pestov, and Todorcevic, Fraïssé limits, Ramsey theory, and topological dynamics of automorphism groups

items.statement: The pointwise-convergence group Aut(U_Q^<), and every finite point stabilizer required by its finite-support permutation model, is extremely amenable.
items.proof_plan: The age of U_Q^< is the rigid class of finite linearly ordered rational metric spaces. Apply Nešetřil's Ramsey theorem to this age, then KPT Theorem 4.7 to its Fraïssé limit, obtaining extreme amenability. For a finite support E, the point stabilizer is the automorphism group of the Fraïssé expansion with constants for E; its age remains rigid and Ramsey by coloring expansions over the fixed finite substructure, so KPT applies again. Feed this exact stabilizer conclusion, not merely extreme amenability of the full group, to the preceding BPI theorem.

items.title: Corson's Stone obstruction is ordinal boundable

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: The sentence asserting a Q-valued metric space with an open cover having no point-finite refinement is ordinal boundable, with Corson's explicit absolute bound omega+41, and has an atom-blind typed transfer certificate.
items.proof_plan: Reproduce Lemma 5 constructor by constructor: code the underlying atom set, Q-valued metric, rational balls, open cover, candidate refinements, functions and point-finiteness within the stated iterates of the relative hierarchy, ending at V_{omega+41}(A). Relativization captures every possible refinement, not only a chosen one. All atomic tests are equality/membership on carried sorts and the pure rational parameter is fixed, so the formula is atom-blind and meets the typed Jech-Sochor/Pincus certificate.

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI with failure of Stone's theorem

references.title: Samuel Corson, The Independence of Stone's Theorem from the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+BPI with a metrizable nonmetacompact space is consistent.
items.proof_plan: In Corson's ZFA permutation model, the full finite-stabilizer extreme-amenability chain gives BPI and Theorem 1 gives the bad rational metric space. Lemma 5 supplies the omega+41 bound and atom-blind certificate. Apply the proof-bearing Pincus transfer theorem to BPI plus this sentence, then the formal ZFC+GCH and finite-fragment compilers to derive the displayed Con implication. No Recorded Pincus or catalogue item appears in the dependency path.

items.title: Effective metacompactness for discrete metric spaces implies AC

references.title: C. Good, I. J. Tree, and W. S. Watson, On Stone's theorem and the axiom of choice

items.statement: Over ZF, suppose that for every discrete metrizable space X and every open cover U of X there exist a point-finite open refinement V and a map a:V→U such that V⊆a(V) for every V∈V. Then AC holds.
items.proof_plan: Reproduce Good-Tree-Watson Proposition 5. Start with an arbitrary pairwise-disjoint family F of nonempty sets (using tagged copies first if necessary) and give X=F union union F the discrete metric. Cover X by U={{x,F}:x∈F∈F}. Apply the per-cover existential hypothesis once to obtain a point-finite refinement V together with its witnessing map a:V→U; no global refinement operator is assumed. For each F, the definable family C(F)={V∈V:F∈V} is nonempty because V covers X and finite because V is point-finite. Then f(F)={x∈F:there is V∈C(F) with a(V)={x,F}} is a nonempty finite subset of F: every V in C(F) is contained in a(V), so a(V) is one of the displayed pairs through F. Thus f is a Multiple Choice function, and the preceding ZF equivalence yields AC.

items.title: Products of cofinite spaces are compact exactly under BPI

references.title: Kyriakos Keremedis and Eleftherios Tachtsis, Wallman Compactifications and Tychonoff's Compactness Theorem in ZF

items.statement: Over ZF, BPI is equivalent to compactness of every product of cofinite spaces.
items.proof_plan: Follow Proposition 2.13. If the product is empty it is compact. Otherwise fix x in the product. For a family H of closed sets with the finite-intersection property, BPI extends the generated filter to an ultrafilter F. Project F to each cofinite factor and let A_i be the intersection of its closed members. Compactness of the cofinite factor makes A_i nonempty; because A_i is closed it is either the whole factor or finite, and ultrafilter maximality makes a finite A_i a singleton. Choose the unique point in that case and x_i otherwise; this definable point lies in every member of H. Conversely specialize the hypothesis to 2^X, where the two-point cofinite topology is discrete compact Hausdorff; compactness for every X is the published set-ultrafilter/BPI form. No arbitrary-filter encoding is substituted for the source's specialization.

items.title: The isolated-point repair of Kelley's choice space

references.title: Eric Schechter, Handbook of Analysis and Its Foundations, compact T1 product equivalence

items.statement: For a nonempty set A, the topological sum X_A=A_c plus {infinity}, where A_c has the cofinite topology and infinity is isolated, is compact T1 and A_c is a closed subspace. This is the corrected Kelley coordinate.
items.proof_plan: The cofinite space A_c is compact in ZF: take one member of an open cover containing any fixed a in A; its finite complement is covered by finitely many further members using finite choice. It is T1 because singletons are closed. Adding the isolated one-point compact summand preserves compactness and T1 by a two-piece finite-subcover argument. The coordinate constraint A_c is closed because its complement {infinity} is open. Contrast this with A inside the one-point cofinite topology on A union {infinity}, where an infinite A with infinite complement need not be closed.

items.title: The compact T1 product theorem is equivalent to AC

references.title: Schechter, Equivalents of the Axiom of Choice

items.statement: Over ZF, AC is equivalent to every product of compact T1 spaces being compact.
items.proof_plan: AC gives product compactness by the published Tychonoff theorem. Conversely, for an arbitrary indexed family (A_i) of nonempty sets form the corrected compact T1 coordinates X_{A_i}. In their product the closed cylinders C_i={x:x_i in A_i} have the finite-intersection property: for a finite J, finite choice selects a_j in A_j and infinity fills every off-J coordinate, defining a point of intersection_{j in J}C_j. Product compactness and the compact-FIP equivalence give a point in intersection_i C_i, whose coordinates form a choice function. Every closedness and FIP supplier is explicit.

items.statement: Over ZF, AC is equivalent to every product of arbitrary compact spaces being compact.
items.proof_plan: AC gives arbitrary Tychonoff. Conversely specialize to compact T1 spaces and apply the preceding equivalence. Include the empty product and do not confuse this with compact Hausdorff products, whose strength is BPI.

items.title: Moore spaces and developments

items.statement: A development is a sequence of open covers whose stars at each point form a neighbourhood base. A Moore space is regular T1 and developable. Finite common refinements normalize a development to be decreasing.
items.proof_plan: Define stars and development; verify finite common refinements are open covers with smaller stars and preserve the neighbourhood-base property. Developments directly give first countability.

items.title: Normalized families and collectionwise normality

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality
Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals

items.statement: A pairwise disjoint family is normalized when every subunion can be separated from its complementary subunion, and separated when it has pairwise disjoint open expansions. Collectionwise normal means every discrete closed family is separated.
items.proof_plan: Fix the closure convention and verify equivalent expansion forms by shrinking. Unions of subfamilies of a discrete closed family are closed, so normality normalizes them; the two-member converse is immediate.

items.title: Metrizable spaces are collectionwise normal

references.title: GMU Math 631 course notes, Axioms of separation
references.locator: Section 14, Theorem 65 and its distance-neighbourhood proof, printed p. 12

items.statement: In ZF, every metrizable space is collectionwise normal.
items.proof_plan: Fix one compatible metric d and a discrete family (F_i) of closed sets; this is one existential witness, not a simultaneous family choice. Put U_i=empty when F_i is empty. For nonempty F_i let H_i=union_{j not equal i}F_j, which is closed because a discrete family is locally finite. If H_i is empty put U_i=X. Otherwise set U_i={x:d(x,F_i)<(1/3)d(x,H_i)}. The two distance functions are 1-Lipschitz, so U_i is open, and discreteness gives each y in F_i a ball avoiding H_i, hence y∈U_i. If x lay in U_i intersect U_j for i not equal j, then F_j⊆H_i and F_i⊆H_j would give d(x,F_i)<d(x,F_j)/3 and d(x,F_j)<d(x,F_i)/3, a contradiction. Thus the U_i are pairwise disjoint open expansions. Empty and singleton families are covered by the explicit cases, and no Choice is used.

items.title: Moore spaces are subparacompact

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem
references.locator: Theorem 2.4 and its proof, printed pp. 2-3

items.statement: In ZFC every Moore space is subparacompact: each open cover has a sigma-discrete closed refinement.
items.proof_plan: Follow Burke Theorem 2.4 with its choice use exposed. Well-order the given cover H={H_alpha:alpha in A}; for a decreasing development G_n put F(alpha,n)={x: H_alpha is the least cover member containing St(x,G_n)} and then replace F(alpha,n) by its closed remainder after all earlier indices. Development gives coverage. The star condition makes each fixed-n remainder family discrete, closedness follows from the earlier-index subtraction and the star test, and every remainder lies in H_alpha. The countable union over n is the required sigma-discrete closed refinement. The well-ordering of H is precisely why this item carries AC rather than claiming a ZF proof.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC well-orders the arbitrary cover

items.title: Collectionwise normal Moore spaces are screenable

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces

items.statement: In ZFC every collectionwise normal Moore space is screenable: every open cover has a refinement that is a countable union of pairwise disjoint open families.
items.proof_plan: For an open cover H, Bing Theorem 9 well-orders H and, using a decreasing development, constructs closed sets x(h,i): a point belongs when h is the first H-member containing it and every development member at level i through it lies in h. Each X_i={x(h,i):h in H} is discrete, refines H, and the union over i covers X. Collectionwise normality expands each X_i to a pairwise disjoint open family Y_i, chosen so each expansion remains inside the corresponding H-member. Therefore union_i Y_i covers X and refines H, so X is screenable exactly as in Bing Theorem 10. The well-order and simultaneous choices are covered by AC.

items.title: Normal screenable Moore spaces are metrizable

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces
references.locator: Theorems 3, 6, 7, and 8 with proofs, printed pp. 178-182

items.statement: In ZFC every normal screenable Moore space is metrizable.
items.proof_plan: Let H be one pairwise-disjoint open layer in a screening, let W=X minus union H, and let G_i be a development. Put X_i={p:no G_i-member containing p meets W}. Normality gives an open D_i containing X_i and disjoint from W; intersecting D_i with the members of H produces a discrete open family H_i, and union_i H_i covers union H. Applying this to every screening layer makes the space strongly screenable (Bing Theorem 8). Screening each development cover by discrete open families makes the space perfectly screenable (Theorem 6). For the countable sequence of discrete open families witnessing perfect screenability, normality supplies the functions F_ij used in Theorem 3; Bing's displayed convergent weighted formula D(x,y), including its sign term R_ij(x,y), satisfies positivity, symmetry, the triangle inequality, and preserves limit points. Hence D is a compatible metric. This retains the complete Theorems 3, 6, 7 and 8 route rather than merely citing the conclusion.

items.title: MA plus not-CH produces an uncountable Q-set

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem
references.locator: Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 with proofs, printed pp. 7-9

items.statement: In ZFC+MA+not-CH, every subset E of the real line of cardinality omega_1 is a Q-set, and hence an uncountable Q-set exists.
items.proof_plan: Fix E={x_alpha:alpha<omega_1} and a countable rational-interval base {W_i}. Refine the base so each pair of distinct points belongs jointly to only finitely many W_i, and let s(x)={i:x in W_i}. Burke Lemma 4.3, proved by the ccc finite-condition poset and the fewer-than-continuum dense sets supplied by MA, says that for every Y subset E there is d subset omega with s(y) almost contained in d for y in Y and s(z) intersect d finite for z in E minus Y. Enumerate d as p(k). Then Y=E intersect intersection_n union_{k>n} W_{p(k)}: almost containment gives membership for y, while finite intersection excludes z. Thus every Y is relatively G-delta. Since not-CH gives omega_1<continuum, the MA hypothesis applies to all required dense families.

items.title: Bing's Q-set space is a normal nonmetrizable Moore space

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem
references.locator: Example 4.1 and its full normality proof, printed pp. 5-7

references.title: R. H. Bing, Metrization of topological spaces

items.statement: For every uncountable Q-set E in the real line, Bing's tangent-disk space Z(E) is a separable normal nonmetrizable Moore space.
items.proof_plan: Use Euclidean disks of radius below 1/n in the upper half-plane and tangent disks at the boundary points to obtain the explicit development; rational upper-half-plane points are dense. The boundary E times {0} is closed and discrete. If Z(E) were metrizable, separability would force every discrete subspace countable, contradicting uncountability. For normality, reduce arbitrary disjoint closed H,K to their boundary traces A,B subset E. The Q-set property writes A and B as decreasing relative G-delta traces of Euclidean open sets S_n,T_n. Burke's construction forms successively thinned tangent-disk unions A_n,B_n whose closures miss the opposite closed set and whose horizontal radii shrink with n; the open unions V=union_n(A_n minus closures of earlier B-layers) and W=union_n(B_n minus closures of earlier A-layers), augmented around the off-axis parts of H,K, contain H,K and are disjoint. The closure estimates in Example 4.1 use exactly S_n intersect E=A and T_n intersect E=B, completing normality.

items.proof_plan: Under the anti-measurable-inner-model hypothesis form the Dodd-Jensen core model K. The covering lemma says every uncountable set of ordinals is contained in a K-set of the same V-cardinality. Since K satisfies GCH, the standard covering calculation at a V-singular strong-limit cardinal gives SCH: choose kappa=beth_delta for a limit delta of cofinality omega, enumerate it by kappa_n=beth_{delta_n}, and obtain 2^kappa=kappa^+. The fine-structural square sequence of K, together with weak covering at this singular kappa, yields square_kappa in V; the standard least-order-type/Fodor extraction from square_kappa gives a stationary E subset kappa^+ of cofinality omega which reflects at no beta<kappa^+. Thus kappa,(kappa_n),E satisfy every displayed HYP clause. This is exactly the Jensen-Dodd input identified by Fleissner on pp. 366-368; it does not attribute an inner-model construction to Fleissner himself.

items.statement: Con(ZFC+NMSC) implies Con(ZFC plus there is a measurable cardinal).
items.proof_plan: The internal theorem gives an inner model M satisfying ZFC plus a measurable cardinal; relativization to M is an interpretation of ZFC+measurable in ZFC+NMSC, which transports derivations, and the verified proof-reduction compiler turns that into the formal Con implication.

items.title: The consistency-strength sandwich for NMSC

references.title: Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals
Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality

items.statement: Con(ZFC+NMSC) implies Con(ZFC plus a measurable cardinal), while Con(ZFC plus a strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC+NMSC); a modern omega-one-strongly compact upper refinement is recorded separately.
items.proof_plan: Keep the internal measurable-inner-model consequence, the formal lower consistency implication and the strongly compact forcing upper implication as three separate claims and chain the latter two.

items.title: The omega-one-strongly compact refinement and open gap

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva, omega-one-strongly compact cardinals and normality

items.statement: Bagaria-da Silva prove Con(ZFC plus an omega-one-strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC+NMSC), via random forcing and PMEA-sigma; whether NMSC reaches that consistency strength is open.
items.proof_plan: Literature context only: Theorem 2.10 gives the pullback, but its Solovay-measure input is sketched and the PMEA-sigma separation modification omitted. It carries no proof load and does not replace the proved strong-compact branch.

title: Normal Moore Spaces, PMEA, and Consistency Strength: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Development stars form a countable local base

references.title: Dennis K. Burke, The Normal Moore Space Problem

items.statement: For metric covers by balls of radius 2^(-n), compute the stars and verify that they form a countable local base.
items.proof_plan: The star contains the radius 2^(-n) ball and is contained in the radius 2^(1-n) ball. Given an epsilon-neighbourhood, choose n with 2^(1-n)<epsilon.

items.title: The three-quarter event calculation in the PMEA proof

references.title: Fremlin, Real-valued-measurable cardinals

items.statement: Two good events of measure above three quarters overlap in positive measure, providing a separating parameter.
items.proof_plan: Compute mu(E intersect F) at least mu(E)+mu(F)-1>1/2, select a point of the overlap, and apply the two opposite closure conditions.

items.title: False: ZFC proves the normal Moore space conjecture

references.title: William G. Fleissner, If all normal Moore spaces are metrizable, then there is an inner model with a measurable cardinal
references.locator: CH instance and complete construction, printed pp. 366-373

items.statement: False relative to Con(ZFC): ZFC proves every normal Moore space metrizable.
items.proof_plan: Con(ZFC) gives Con(ZFC+GCH), hence Con(ZFC+CH); were ZFC to prove NMSC, the fixed NMSC proof and the fixed CH-space proof would compile to a ZFC+CH refutation, hence to a ZFC+GCH refutation, contradicting that consistency implication.
